title: Optimization
summary: A minimization problem specifies a feasible set and objective; its infimum is the optimal value and may be unattained.

context.note: Revision 3 distinguishes the optimization problem, its optimal value, and a minimizer.

assumptions.text: A nonempty feasible set X and an objective f:X→Y are fixed.
The codomain Y has enough order structure for the displayed comparisons and infimum.

content.plain: Optimization first specifies which choices are allowed and how they are scored; the best lower score may or may not be achieved by a choice.
content.exact: A minimization problem is specified by a feasible set X and objective f:X→Y into an ordered codomain. When it exists, inf f(X) is the optimal value. A global minimizer is x*∈X satisfying f(x*)≤f(x) for every x∈X; a finite infimum need not be attained.
content.example: For f(x)=(x−3)² on R, the optimal value is 0 and the unique global minimizer is x=3.
content.caveat: Mathematical optimality is relative to the chosen feasible set, objective, and order; it does not certify that those choices are appropriate.

relations.note: Local and global minimizers quantify over different neighborhoods.
Search procedures may trade current objective value against information gathering.

verification.method: QEVA 0.5 protocol audit corrected scope, assumptions, and dependency semantics; no formal proof is claimed.

provenance.creator: QEVA 0.5 mathematical protocol audit
provenance.source_note: Corrects the former identification of a minimization problem with its infimum. This is an original QEVA formulation and remains subject to independent review.
